ordered_diagnoses: Adenoid cystic carcinoma of the trachea

facts.raw_span: 48-year-old white man
lifelong non-smoker
remote bronchoscopic resection of a tracheal carcinoid 17 years earlier
three-month history of mild hemoptysis
cough without dyspnea
non-tender, 2 × 2 cm subcutaneous mass on his left forearm
oxygen saturation of 94% on room air
normal laboratory studies, including complete blood count, liver and renal function tests, and coagulation profile
polypoid lesion in the precarinal tracheal region adjacent to the anterior wall on chest CT scan
mass arising from the anterior tracheal wall just above the main carina, causing an 80% obstruction of the right main bronchus and 70% obstruction of the left main bronchus on flexible bronchoscopy
tumor consisted of large nests of eosinophilic cells within a collagenous and myxoid matrix on hematoxylin–eosin staining
carcinoid tumor was initially suspected

concepts.why: The patient has a history of remote bronchoscopic resection of a tracheal carcinoid and presents with a new polypoid lesion in the precarinal tracheal region, which is consistent with a recurrent or new tracheal carcinoid tumor.

The polypoid lesion in the precarinal tracheal region and the mass arising from the anterior tracheal wall could be consistent with a tracheal adenoma, although the histological features are more suggestive of a carcinoid tumor.

The polypoid lesion in the precarinal tracheal region and the mass arising from the anterior tracheal wall could be consistent with a tracheal papilloma, although the histological features are not typical of this diagnosis.

The tumor's location and histological features, including large nests of eosinophilic cells within a collagenous and myxoid matrix, could be consistent with a mucoepidermoid carcinoma of the trachea, although this diagnosis is less likely given the patient's history and the initial suspicion of a carcinoid tumor.
